title: The decision-ready PRD
promise: A PRD a reviewer can approve point by point: every change is numbered, stated as a problem, tied to evidence and linked to a switch in the prototype.
gives: One HTML page: numbered points with the evidence beside each, a priority table and a rollout plan.
clipTitle: A PRD you can approve *point by point*
clipLine: Problem, change and evidence. One number per point, everywhere.
when: You have done the research and need a decision, not a discussion.
Reviewers skim, so the problem list has to be readable from the headings alone.
Several small changes are travelling together and each needs its own yes or no.
skip: You have no evidence yet. Run the teardown or the synthesis first. This skill will not invent a problem.
It is a single bug fix. Write a ticket.
You need an engineering design. This says what and why, and leaves how to the team.

inputs.name: Evidence
inputs.note: A teardown, a synthesis, a pre-mortem or your own notes. Anything a point can cite.

inputs.name: The product today
inputs.note: Screens or a description of the current behaviour.

inputs.name: Constraints
inputs.note: Rules, dependencies and dates you already know about.

outputs.name: prd.html
outputs.note: The document: section nav, a summary grid and one card per point.

outputs.name: prd.json
outputs.note: The same as data. The prototype skill builds one switch per point from it.

steps.title: List problems before solutions
steps.body: Each point's title is the problem as a user meets it. If the problem cannot be stated from the evidence, the point is cut.

steps.title: Number everything once
steps.body: Section N, point N.n. The same IDs are used in the priority table, the rollout plan and the prototype.

steps.title: Write Problem and Change, two sentences each
steps.body: The change is a concrete move on a screen, often with the exact words the user would read.

steps.title: Put the evidence beside the claim
steps.body: Each point shows the product today, a reference and the proposal, and names the source.

steps.title: Make constraints first-class
steps.body: Rules, dependencies and risks from the pre-mortem get their own labelled callout on the point they affect. Never a footnote.

steps.title: Say how you would know
steps.body: Each point names a baseline to measure, the movement expected and the signal that would mean stop.

steps.title: Order the rollout by reason
steps.body: A table of what ships when, and why then.

checks.name: Every point has a problem, a change and evidence
checks.note: The checker fails a point with any of the three missing.

checks.name: IDs are unique and used consistently
checks.note: Every ID in the priority and rollout tables must exist as a point, and every point must appear in the rollout.

checks.name: Titles state problems
checks.note: A title that opens with a verb such as Add or Build is rejected, so it gets rewritten as what the user faces today.

checks.name: Every point says how you would know
checks.note: Baseline, expected movement and stop signal are required.

checks.name: Every figure has a source or is marked as an estimate
checks.note: A number in a point with no source is flagged in the output.

checks.name: The first release is small enough to ship
checks.note: Read the first rollout row and ask what you would cut.

failures.title: Tidy structure can hide thin evidence
failures.body: A numbered card looks authoritative even when it rests on one quote.
failures.catch: Each point shows how many sources it rests on. Challenge anything resting on one.

failures.title: Expected movement is a guess
failures.body: The skill will not invent a figure, so it writes a direction and a reason. That is honest, and it is still a guess.
failures.catch: Replace the directions with your own baselines before the review.

failures.title: It cannot see your politics
failures.body: The rollout order reflects effort and constraints, not who has to agree.
failures.catch: Reorder the rollout yourself. The IDs keep everything else in step.

tangelo.label: Tangelo: the weekly shop PRD
tangelo.note: Six points in three sections, a priority table and a rollout plan.
tangelo.ask: Write the PRD for the weekly shop from the teardown, the synthesis and the pre-mortem.
tangelo.demoNote: The agent reads three pieces of research and writes six numbered points. Watch the evidence land beside each claim. When it ends, scroll the document yourself.

run.by: Written alongside the skill as its reference example, then revised to match what the teardown, synthesis and pre-mortem runs actually found.
run.note: This is the one example here that was not produced by a fresh agent session. The checker found one fault in the first draft, a figure not marked as an estimate, which is fixed.

carousel.title: Three pieces of research *in*
carousel.body: A teardown, an interview synthesis and a pre-mortem. The PRD cites all three by name.

carousel.title: The problem first, *evidence beside it*
carousel.body: Every point states what happens today, the change, and the screen or quote that supports it.

carousel.title: One number *per point*
carousel.body: Point 2.1 is 2.1 in the tables, in the rollout plan and in the prototype.

carousel.title: A table you can *argue with*
carousel.body: What each point moves, how big it is, and what it is waiting on.

carousel.title: What ships first, *and why*
carousel.body: A rollout in three steps. Each step says why it goes where it does.

larkspur.label: Larkspur: the Share by link PRD
larkspur.note: Six points in three sections, a priority table and a rollout in four steps.
larkspur.ask: Write the PRD for replacing Team suggestions with Share by link, from the teardown, the synthesis and the pre-mortem.
larkspur.demoNote: The agent reads the teardown, the synthesis and the pre-mortem, then writes six numbered points for Share by link. Watch the evidence land beside each claim. When it ends, scroll the document yourself.

run.by: A fresh agent session with only the skill folder and the inputs
run.note: The checker failed the first draft: point 2.2 quoted the trial promise in full, and the two quoted sentences were counted against its length. The run reworded it and passed, which showed that the rule to quote exact words and the rule to stay short can clash.

vireo.label: Vireo: the draft-first recap PRD
vireo.note: Six points in three sections, a priority table and a rollout in three steps.
vireo.ask: Write the PRD for replacing Auto-assign with a draft-first recap with sources. I need to make the decision this week.
vireo.demoNote: The agent reads the synthesis, the teardown and the pre-mortem, then writes six numbered points for a draft-first recap. Watch the evidence land beside each claim. When it ends, scroll the document yourself.

run.by: A fresh agent session with only the skill folder and the inputs
run.note: The checker failed the first draft: point 2.1 gave the 2 point lift worth shipping as if it were a forecast. The run moved the figure and labelled it a plan setting, and noted that the check reads one field only, so it can be dodged.
